answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, time-bounded tasks, with each result checked against independent peers and a public beacon of task assignments. Repeatedly passing as new identities does not multiply influence: the same scarce tasks and review capacity limit how many accounts one operator can sustain, while missed deadlines or inconsistent work lose the stake bonded to each account. The quill records outcomes, and the reef of peer checks makes cheap identity creation costly in time, collateral, and coordination.
